text: {"answer":"The evidence suggests routine daily vitamin D supplementation is not beneficial for most adults who are already vitamin D replete. Large trials (VITAL, ViDA, D2d, over 30,000 participants) found no prevention of cancer, cardiovascular events, falls or type 2 diabetes in replete adults [fbce4d7a6120#1]. Systematic reviews of fracture prevention found little to no effect from vitamin D supplements alone [53bc338e3607#3], and a US task force recommends against vitamin D and calcium for fracture prevention in healthy postmenopausal women [9c98e4515e3d#0]. The contradicting side is weaker but real: some guidelines still recommend supplementation for falls or fractures despite these reviews [9c98e4515e3d#0], post hoc analyses suggest modest benefits for deficient individuals [fbce4d7a6120#3], and correcting severe deficiency is considered essential [fbce4d7a6120#4]. Supplementation is also recommended for at-risk groups such as older adults and those with limited sun exposure [7aabe982f481#1][691df7883190#4]. Overall, targeted supplementation for deficiency or at-risk people makes sense, while daily use by replete adults lacks support.","confidence":70,"one_line":"Routine daily vitamin D for replete adults shows no clear benefit; supplementation is justified for deficiency or at-risk groups."}
